title: Tom Anderson's cabarets and Paul Dominguez
summary: Asked about Storyville cabarets, he says he played for Tom Anderson and for Paul Dominguez, who had cabarets on Rampart-area streets, and describes the bandstands and the crowds.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Tell us some more about those clubs over in Storyville. Like what is Tom Anderson's like inside?

He means in the district. Oh! I played with Anderson. I played with him. I played with him on the right part between Canal and Abraville. On that side of the back. Anderson. I played with him. I mean this fellow, Paul Dominguez. I know him at Dwyer. You know him? He heard all of him. He did Paul Dyer too, you know. Paul Dominguez? What's Paul then? I didn't know that. Yeah, since Paul Dyer, he was a good bass player. He was the one who gave me a friendly good actor. He played violin too. Oh yeah, Paul used to play violin. Well, he didn't know his brother. Andre. He was pitching the paper. He knew he said a lot. But anyhow. Is it a cabaret? Yeah, he had a cabaret on Grand Falls Street. He had one on Abraville. That was the last one he had on Grand Falls Street. He had one back on Abraville, St. Robinson, and Claybourne right behind the desk. That side had a big place there. Nice place in Chisholm. Way in New York, you know.
Yeah. Well, I used to play that for him too.
What were those places like inside? A lot of decorations?
